Unlike sibling methods such as [Deformation Network for 4D Gaussian Splatting](16173-deformation-network-for-4d-gaussian-splatting.md) or [VolSegGS](10433-volseggs.md) which optimize existing Gaussians, GSDeformer explicitly subdivides ellipsoids to handle complex curvature [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states that GSDeformer is a cage-based deformation algorithm that builds a proxy point cloud from Gaussians and transfers deformation back to 3DGS. It specifically mentions 'splitting the relevant Gaussians to handle bending' and notes that 'Simply optimizing the existing Gaussians, as proposed by ARAP-GS or VRGS, is insufficient for accurately modeling bending.' The text further explains that splitting is essential for handling large deformations (complex curvature/bending) and that disabling splitting causes spiking artifacts. This directly supports the claim that GSDeformer explicitly subdivides ellipsoids (Gaussians) to handle complex curvature, unlike methods that only optimize existing Gaussians.
